what: Q126(c) second pass: the four flip energies refitted on job (b)'s toggle recount, at every rung of its ladder, on the same 14 measured board powers and the same two bases as the first pass -- plus a verification of what the first pass published. NOTHING HERE TOUCHES THE FROZEN PREDICTIONS OR THEIR SCORES: a recount changes the price per counted event, not the watts.

verification_of_the_first_pass.what: the first pass's toggle_recount_refit, re-run against the files as they stand now. Job (b)'s d1059a8e landed after it was written.

settled_over_hf.why: rung 'settled_over_hf' is retired. hier-factors.json's own _how_to_use now says: 'Do NOT divide by_block_settled by the per-module factors below' -- 12 of the 40 switching modules hold no merged net at all and carry a null factor, and 7 more are attribution artefacts. Use 'hier_one_factor', which is the recipe that file gives instead.
settled_over_hf.what_it_did_before_the_guard: it divided by_block_settled by hier-factors.json's per-module factor; 12 of the 40 modules now carry a null factor, so the divide raised TypeError
settled_over_hf.hier_factors_now_says: For a refit, use recount.json key <pattern>.mean.nets_hier directly; it exists for every pattern measured here and needs no factor. To split that total into price classes, take the SHARES from by_block_settled (names, attributed to the module where the net switches) and scale the whole unit by _total -- one factor for the unit. Do NOT divide by_block_settled by the per-module factors below, and do NOT use by_block_hier as a per-block net count: under the hierarchy merge a net is credited to the OUTERMOST module that names it, so the multiplier's share reads 54.8% of by_block_settled but 22.8% of by_block_hier on randn and 0.0% on pow2 and signs. A per-module pass also leaves the 12 unfactored modules undivided (mixing name counts into a net total) and crushes the 7 flagged ones to near zero.
settled_over_hf.read_instead: the hier_one_factor rung below, which is the recipe hier-factors.json now gives

bench.how: the bench's own coverage counts, toggles.json -- what every published fJ was fitted on

settled.how: recount.json nets_settled, split by by_block_settled: one count per RTL NAME, after the settling window drops the transient values Verilator's coverage counter keeps

ids.how: recount.json nets_ids: once per VCD identifier, names that share a waveform object merged

hier.how: per pattern, nets_hier as the total with the SHARES taken from by_block_settled -- job (b)'s corrected recipe, applied pattern by pattern

hier_one_factor.how: by_block_settled scaled by ONE factor for the whole unit, hier-factors.json _total (5.327 settled names per merged net on randn) -- job (b)'s corrected recipe read literally, 'scale the whole unit by one factor'

distinct.how: per pattern, nets_distinct as the total, shares from by_block_settled: once per distinct waveform, job (b)'s LOWER BOUND on the physical count

distinct_one_factor.how: by_block_settled scaled by ONE factor, randn's nets_settled / nets_distinct

hier_by_block.how: by_block_hier straight. KEPT ONLY FOR THE RECORD: this is what the first pass read, and hier-factors.json now says a net is credited to the OUTERMOST module that names it, so by_block_hier is not a per-block net count. It is what made the multiplier price come out negative

cross_check_against_the_open_netlist.reading: the board-power fit puts about 3.7-3.8x the energy on one multiply-add that the netlist's own power analysis does, which is the size of everything the board meter sees and the lane's nets are not: the rest of the die that scales with the kernel, and the board's own conversion. A 'per wire' number taken from board watts is an upper bound on a wire by about that factor.

capacitance_convention: E = 0.5 C V^2 for one counted transition at V_REF = 0.517 V, so C_fF = 2 E_fJ / V^2 = 7.483 fF per fJ. A toggle is one edge here, so a full 0->1->0 cycle costs C V^2 and counts twice.
